newsitem.title: UK: NatWest down in weak UK bank sector.
newsitem.headline: NatWest down in weak UK bank sector.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc shares fell on Thursday, echoing losses in U.S. banks overnight, dealers said.
Lower quotes offered by market-makers for UK bank stock, in anticipation of profit-taking after their recent rally,also added to downward pressure, dealers said.

NatWest shares dropped 19p to 773p by 0835 GMT, though dealers said sizeable sellers had so far failed to emerge. "If we see real profit-taking, then I think the sector will go a lot lower," said one.
Elsewhere among the banks, Barclays Plc dropped 15p to 12.00 stg, Abbey National Plc fell 13p to 914p, Lloyds TSB Group Plc declined 10-1/2p to 599p and Royal Bank of Scotland Plc fell 6p to 606p.
One dealer said weakness in U.S. bank stocks overnight in New York undermined UK banks.

He cited worries that the possible relaxation of the 1933 Glass Steagall banking act, that prevents cross-ownership of financial institutions, could prompt a spending spree by banks in the United States.
In New York, Citicorp fell $2-7/8 to $116-3/4, Chase Manhattan dropped $3-1/8 to $93-1/8, Morgan Stanley weakened $1-3/4 to $65-7/8 and JP Morgan declined $1-3/8 to $103-7/8.

Last year NatWest bought leading U.S. Treasury bond broker-dealer Greenwich Capital Holdings Inc for $590 million (385 million stg) and the mergers and acquisitions specialist Gleacher for $135 million, but analysts are not expecting NatWest to make any further acquisitions in the U.S. in the short term.
